concerns.text: T004a-Backoff is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T006a-MP-Availability-Check ('Depends on T006a for MP availability flag'). T006a must run BEFORE T004a to set the global flag. This creates a hidden sequential dependency that violates the [P] tag and the parallel execution model implied by Phase 2.

T004a-LogSchema is marked [P] but depends on T004a-Backoff ('Depends on T004a-Backoff'). Since T004a-Backoff is also marked [P], this implies they can run in parallel, which is impossible as the log schema implementation relies on the backoff logic being present. T004a-LogSchema must be sequential to T004a-Backoff.

T006b-DataFetch and T006d-DataFetch-MP are marked [P] but depend on T004a-Backoff ('Depends on T004a-Backoff (interface)'). If T004a-Backoff is [P] and runs in parallel with these, the downloaders may attempt to use the backoff logic before it is implemented/initialized. These tasks must be sequential to T004a-Backoff.

T0049, T050, T051 are marked [P] but depend on T004a-Backoff, T004c, T006b, T006d. The 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section explicitly states 'T049, T050, T051 must be implemented and verified before T047a/T047b' and 'T049 and T050 depend on T004a-Backoff... (cannot run in parallel with them)'. Marking them [P] contradicts the explicit sequential constraints defined in the text.

T006a-MP-Availability-Check is marked [P] but the text states 'Must be completed BEFORE T004a-Backoff'. If T004a-Backoff is [P] and runs in parallel with other Phase 2 tasks, T006a must also be sequential to T004a-Backoff to ensure the flag is set. The [P] tag is misleading here.

The 'Checkpoint' text states 'Foundation is READY ONLY AFTER T006b-DataFetch, T006d-DataFetch-MP, T007, T007b, T008a, T008b, T006c, T004a-Backoff, T004a-LogSchema, T004b, T004c, T006a are complete'. However, the [P] tags on T004a-Backoff, T004a-LogSchema, T004b, T004c, T006a, T006b, T006d suggest they can run in parallel, which contradicts the explicit dependency chain (T006a -> T004a -> T006b/T006d) described in the task descriptions.
